sources.gender-odd-one-out: S04: maskil femminil.pdf, exercise 6, excluding row 4

provenance.corrections: Context Q4 requests the feminine counterpart of patri; Q6 requires tfajla with It-; Q8 opening simplified to Darba raġel. Adjective mgerfex and odd-word row moħor are withheld.

editorialReview.method: Editorially reviewed source tasks; contradictory and ambiguous prompts corrected or withheld before publication.

items.prompt: Is-____ beda jidden filgħodu kmieni. Write the masculine of tiġieġa.
items.explanation: Is-serduq is the rooster. The rooster began crowing early in the morning.

items.prompt: ____ iżżewġet is-sena l-oħra. Write the feminine of ħija.
items.explanation: Oħti means my sister: My sister got married last year.

items.prompt: Il-____ tiegħi dejjem tpaċpaċ man-nies. Write the feminine of ġar.
items.explanation: Il-ġara tiegħi is my female neighbour. The verb tpaċpaċ agrees with her.

items.prompt: Is-____ tgħix f'kunvent tal-klawsura. Write the feminine counterpart of patri.
items.explanation: Is-soru is the nun. The feminine tgħix agrees with soru. Patri and soru name corresponding religious roles.

items.prompt: Il-____ beda jinħaq. Write the masculine of ħmara.
items.explanation: Il-ħmar beda jinħaq: The donkey began braying.

items.prompt: It-____ xtrat tibdila ġdida. Write a feminine counterpart of ġuvni that fits the supplied article.
items.explanation: It-tfajla fits the given article. Xebba would require Ix-xebba, so it cannot fill this unchanged sentence.

items.prompt: Ir-____ sellem lin-nies. Write the masculine of reġina.
items.explanation: Ir-re is the king: The king greeted the people.

items.prompt: Darba raġel salva ____ milli tegħreq fil-Port il-Kbir. Write the feminine of bodbod.
items.explanation: Mogħża means a nanny goat. The feminine tegħreq agrees with this referent.

items.prompt: ____ ħaditni sal-bandli. Write the feminine of missieri.
items.explanation: Ommi means my mother: My mother took me to the swings.

items.prompt: In-____ kienet se tintilef. Write the feminine of muntun.
items.explanation: In-nagħġa is the ewe. The feminine kienet agrees with her.

items.prompt: L-____ kien joqgħod waħdu. Write the masculine of armla.
items.explanation: L-armel is the widower. Notice the stem change armel / armla.

items.prompt: Is-Sur Meli kellu ____. Write the masculine counterpart of debba.
items.explanation: Żiemel means horse, or stallion in this male/female contrast; debba means mare.

items.prompt: Write the feminine singular of twil (tall / long).
items.explanation: Twil changes to twila.

items.prompt: Write the feminine singular of mħawwad (confused / mixed up).
items.explanation: Mħawwad changes to mħawda, not just an unchanged stem plus -a.

items.prompt: Write the feminine singular of mgħawweġ (crooked / bent).
items.explanation: Mgħawweġ changes to mgħawġa.

items.prompt: Write the feminine singular of mxarrab (wet).
items.explanation: Mxarrab changes to mxarrba.

items.prompt: Write the feminine singular of mħassar (erased / cancelled / spoiled).
items.explanation: Mħassar changes to mħassra. The precise English meaning depends on context.

items.prompt: Write the feminine singular of mkisser (broken).
items.explanation: Mkisser changes to mkissra.

items.prompt: Write the feminine singular of mfarrak (shattered / smashed).
items.explanation: Mfarrak changes to mfarrka.

items.prompt: nsiet: identify the third-person singular past-tense form.
items.explanation: Nsiet means she forgot.

items.prompt: beka: identify the third-person singular past-tense form.
items.explanation: Beka means he cried.

items.prompt: mexxa: identify the third-person singular past-tense form.
items.explanation: Mexxa means he led / moved something.

items.prompt: xandret: identify the third-person singular past-tense form.
items.explanation: Xandret means she broadcast / announced.

items.prompt: siefer: identify the third-person singular past-tense form.
items.explanation: Siefer means he travelled abroad.

items.prompt: hedded: identify the third-person singular past-tense form.
items.explanation: Hedded means he threatened.

items.prompt: mejlet: identify the third-person singular past-tense form.
items.explanation: Mejlet means she leaned / tilted.

items.prompt: sawret: identify the third-person singular past-tense form.
items.explanation: Sawret means she shaped / formed.

items.prompt: rebaħ: identify the third-person singular past-tense form.
items.explanation: Rebaħ means he won.

items.prompt: mesħet: identify the third-person singular past-tense form.
items.explanation: Mesħet means she wiped.

items.prompt: Which noun is feminine?
items.explanation: Soru (nun) is feminine; the other three nouns here are masculine.

items.prompt: Which form is masculine among these feminine forms?
items.explanation: Mar means he went. Stħajlet and bierket are she-forms here; żagħżugħa refers to a young woman.

items.prompt: Which third-person singular past-tense verb form is masculine?
items.explanation: Miet means he died; the other forms here are third-person feminine singular.

items.prompt: Which form is feminine among these masculine forms?
items.explanation: Sewda is the feminine singular of iswed (black).
